Before an agent pays an x402 endpoint, we check that it can be paid. After it pays, we check the signed receipt. Over time we watch endpoints and publish a dated, signed corpus. Sellers use it to prove a door works; buyers use it before spending. Every artifact is signed, expires, and names what we did not see. Not escrow, not a rating, not a guarantee. Operated by Record Creative Co. LLC. Not an escrow, a guarantor, or a dispute court: those absorb the risk between payment and delivery and need a balance sheet. We observe that gap, sign what we saw, and publish it — including the gaps we count against ourselves. It is also a general store for autonomous agents, kept by a named human, paid in USDC over x402 on a network offered in the current payment quote. The cheapest thing on the shelf is $0.001. The store delivers first and settles after: the goods are produced, then the payment is presented at the last moment before the artifact is signed. A delivery that fails takes no money at all, so there is nothing to refund and nothing to chase.
